[[File:Star Trek CCG First Edition original logo.png|thumb|right|180px|Original Star Trek CCG First Edition logo.]]
[[File:Star Trek TNG CCG card back.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Card back, ''Star Trek: The Next Generation'' CCG (Decipher, 1994).]]
The '''''Star Trek'' Customizable Card Game''' ('''Star Trek CCG''') was [[Decipher]]'s first customizable card game. [[Tom Braunlich]] and [[Rollie Tesh]] designed it. Decipher released it in 1994 as ''Star Trek: The Next Generation'' Customizable Card Game.<ref name="st-timeline">Kathy McCracken, [http://decipher.com/content/2004/st10/sttimeline.html The History of Star Trek CCG: The Timeline], Decipher (2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080821113824/http://decipher.com/content/2004/st10/sttimeline.html Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="wp-stccg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Trek_Customizable_Card_Game Star Trek Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260927114824/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Trek_Customizable_Card_Game Internet Archive].</ref> In 2002 Decipher relaunched the game as Second Edition.<ref name="wp-stccg" /> Franklin Kenter won the 2002 World Championship at [[DecipherCon 2002]] over John Corbett.<ref name="st-day3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021106035232/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/1102stccgstandings.html Star Trek CCG World Championship Day Three], Kathy McCracken, Decipher Daily News (2 November 2002)</ref>

Players scored by completing missions and solving dilemmas along a spaceline of locations.<ref name="duelist3">Deanna Dusbabek, "Star Trek: The Next Generation Customizable Card Game", ''The Duelist'' 3 (Fall 1994), pp. 50–51. [https://archive.org/details/DuelistMagazineIssue3 Internet Archive].</ref> Braunlich and Tesh called location-based play "the central element of all of our CCGs".<ref name="rfd14">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=279s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 4:39–6:44. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref> Living on Bainbridge Island near Wizards of the Coast, they met ''Magic: The Gathering'' designer [[Richard Garfield]] and told Wizards they would not copy ''Magic''.<ref name="bp27">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zK_94pNOPTU&t=546s The Booster Pack #27 — The making of the Star Trek CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (10 August 2022), 9:06–10:30. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20221006131804/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zK_94pNOPTU Internet Archive].</ref>

== Relation to SWCCG ==

Work on [[Star Wars CCG]] began right after the ''Star Trek'' launch, before the ''Star Wars'' license was signed.<ref name="bp-start">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=186s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 3:06–4:40. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261023013204/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=186s Internet Archive (watch page)].</ref> Braunlich moved to the ''Star Wars'' game before the ''Star Trek'' game was finished.<ref name="bp27" />

SWCCG kept several ''Star Trek'' ideas: 60-card decks, film stills as card art, a row of locations, a split between "noun" cards (characters and locations) and "verb" cards (interrupts), and a policy of not rotating old cards out.<ref name="bp27" />

[[Bill Martinson]] later led design of the ''Star Trek'' game. He also edited SWCCG card text with [[Warren Holland]].<ref name="darcy-dag">[https://www.kendallcast.ninja/2021/11/jerry-darcy-on-dagobah.html Jerry Darcy on Dagobah], KendallCast (2 November 2021). Audio: [https://archive.org/details/jerry-darcy-on-dagobah Internet Archive]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009004205/https://www.kendallcast.ninja/2021/11/jerry-darcy-on-dagobah.html Internet Archive].</ref>

== Editions ==

[[File:Star Trek CCG Second Edition original logo.png|thumb|right|180px|Original Star Trek CCG Second Edition logo.]]

Decipher released ''All Good Things'' for First Edition in July 2003 and the physical ''Enterprise Collection'' in July 2006.<ref name="trek-one-products">[https://www.trekcc.org/1e/?pool=traditional First Edition: Traditional card pool], The Continuing Committee, physical release list. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261107204314/https://swccg.com/snapshots/trekcc/1e-traditional.html Internet Archive].</ref>

The original Second Edition rulebook credits [[Evan Lorentz]], [[Brad DeFruiter]] and [[Tim Ellington]] with design.<ref name="trek-original-rules">[https://galacticempires.no-ip.org/CCGST1E/rules/2eRulebook_v1.pdf Star Trek Customizable Card Game Second Edition Rulebook], Decipher, original edition, p. 30. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261107200226/https://galacticempires.no-ip.org/CCGST1E/rules/2eRulebook_v1.pdf Internet Archive].</ref> Decipher released Second Edition on 18 December 2002. Its last physical expansion, ''What You Leave Behind'', appeared on 14 December 2007.<ref name="trek-two-products">[https://www.trekcc.org/2e/ Second Edition: Set list], The Continuing Committee, physical release list. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20250605154046/https://www.trekcc.org/2e/ Internet Archive].</ref> In Second Edition, players staff ships, overcome dilemmas chosen by the opponent and complete missions for points.<ref name="trek-original-rules" />

== Playing online ==

[[TCGMix]] offers separate browser versions of [https://tcgmix.com/startrek/ First Edition]<ref name="trek-first-online">[https://tcgmix.com/startrek/ Star Trek CCG First Edition on TCGMix]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261107193612/https://tcgmix.com/startrek/ Internet Archive].</ref> and [https://tcgmix.com/startrek2e/ Second Edition].<ref name="trek-second-online">[https://tcgmix.com/startrek2e/ Star Trek CCG Second Edition on TCGMix]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261107193854/https://tcgmix.com/startrek2e/ Internet Archive].</ref>
